package.display_name: The house fill graphs - one per room

purpose: The node-by-node contract for the three PCG fill graphs, with the parameters each node needs, so the graphs can be built once and stay consistent between rooms.

authority.fill_contract: specs/p0/melusina_house_p0_fill.v1.json (the species rows, the densities, the exclusions and the rules)
authority.host_graph: Content/EnvSandbox/PCG/House/PCG_MelusinaRoomShell_PCGex.uasset - the fill graph is a SUBGRAPH of this, so it inherits the shell's bounds instead of guessing them

shared_structure.one_graph_per_room: or one graph with three room subgraphs; either way the node chain below is identical and only the volume, the density and the species rows change
shared_structure.subgraph_of_the_shell: the fill graph lives inside PCG_MelusinaRoomShell_PCGex as a subgraph, so the room's interior bounds come from the shell's own bounds source
shared_structure.preview: the PCG editor preview shows the spawn live, so the density texture is painted while the room is visible

node_chain.role: the room's interior bounds, inherited from the shell subgraph
node_chain.parameters: room-specific: the shell's own bounds, never a hand-typed box

node_chain.role: the room's named dressing surfaces, authored by the artist
node_chain.parameters: one spline per surface; the spline carries the surface NAME as an attribute

node_chain.role: sample the surfaces for scatter; the grid covers the floor on the 0.6 m module
node_chain.parameters: Surface Sampler: the splines from step 2, 0.5 m spacing. Grid Sampler: 60 cm cells over the room bounds. Both must publish a UV attribute for the room's local XY - the texture sample needs it.

node_chain.role: pull the room's density texture into the graph
node_chain.parameters: SourceType = TexturePath; SourceAttributeName = 'AssetPath' (a point attribute holding the texture path); Filter = Bilinear; Transform = the room's XY bounds; TexelSize = 50 cm; ColorChannel = R (NOT the default Alpha)
UVSource = the UV attribute from step 3; the sampled value is written into $Density

node_chain.role: cull the points the field says nothing about
node_chain.parameters: LowerBound = 0.05, UpperBound = 1.0, bKeepZeroDensityPoints = false. This node filters the $Density attribute - there is no density asset to point it at.

node_chain.role: choose the species per point, weighted by the density
node_chain.parameters: Mode = WeightModulation ('more density prefers the higher-weight species'); DensitySource = $Density; DensityInfluence = 1.0; OutOfRangePolicy = Clamp; the per-entry weights are the fill contract's species rows
overlap resolution by pulling, sample count 2

node_chain.role: cull everything the walk or the beat must not share
node_chain.parameters: the exclusion sources listed under exclusions
mesh + material instance from the fill contract's species row; rotation rule per species; the mesh MUST be the converted Enchanted Interiors instance on M_Master_Toon_Universal

bedroom.fill_budget: no more than 3 fill species legible in any one frame

landing.fill_budget: the landing is a threshold, not a room - keep it sparse

salon.fill_budget: the M04 landmark (the medallion and its five rings) must stay legible: the fill keeps out of the medallion footprint

exclusions.rule: the walk corridor plus a 4 m buffer - the P0 score says the walk must never snag on furniture
exclusions.note: the derived density textures already have this corridor cut from the reconstructed route; the graph's own spline filter is the authoritative one

exclusions.rule: the medallion and its five concentric rings stay clear
the fill never crowds a hand-placed prop

exclusions.source: the walls and the door swings
the stair run and the stair newels
exclusions.rule: the grand staircase is framed, not walkable

density_texture_import.why: a PCGDensityData samples a Texture2D, so the PNG has to become an asset with the right settings - a colour texture would wash the field out

recipe.filter: Default (bilinear) - the field is meant to be smooth
recipe.address: Clamp - the field must not tile at the room edges

density_texture_import.uv_convention: the texture's X maps to world X and its Y maps to world Y over the room's volume, with V increasing towards +Y (UE textures are top-down origin by default, so the import must be flipped on V)
density_texture_import.helper: Content/Python/melodia_house_fill_import.py - the artist runs it in the editor with the level open. It imports the three PNGs with this recipe and creates the three PCGDensityData assets. It is NOT run by an agent: it writes into Content/ and the editor belongs to the artist.

graph_settings.bGenerated: true - the fill regenerates on demand
graph_settings.cleanup: the fill is additive: regenerating removes the actors IT created and never touches anything else
graph_settings.seed: the room's seed from the kit (RoomKit.Seed) so a room is reproducible
graph_settings.runtime_generation: off for now - a shipping level bakes the fill; the decision is W8

verification: the graph runs in the PCG preview and the spawn is visible
a screenshot of each room shows no more than 3 fill species legible
the audit re-run after the fill reports 0 issues and the contract placements have not moved
the dressing census is byte-identical before and after a regeneration (the fill is additive)
not_yet_true: no node in this contract has been built - it is a design contract
the density textures are a derived first pass and still need the artist's paint
the shell's graph does not yet publish the named surfaces as scene proxies
the import helper is written but never run: the editor belongs to the artist

mechanism_correction.found: 2026-10-22, by reading the UE 5.8 PCG plugin headers
mechanism_correction.wrong_before: the contract said a PCGVolume carries a PCGDensityData asset and that the old density volume is deprecated
true_now: APCGVolume is an AVolume with a UPCGComponent and carries NO density asset
there is no PCGDensityData class in this engine build
the density is a $Density ATTRIBUTE inside the graph, produced by PCGExGetTextureData -> PCGExSampleTexture
the species choice is weighted by the density with PCGExSelectorDensityWeighted
mechanism_correction.the_gotcha: PCGExGetTextureData's ColorChannel defaults to ALPHA; a grayscale density texture carries its value in RGB with alpha = 1, so the channel must be R or the field reads 1.0 everywhere and every point survives the filter
